2. In Figures 2 and 3, TMEM175 deficiency demonstrates anti-tumour effects by
impeding tumour growth and metastasis, with concurrent alterations in tumour-
associated macrophage (TAM) composition and T-cell infiltration. These findings,
however, are predominantly observational. A mechanistic elucidation is necessary
to substantiate whether, and through what pathways, TMEM175 deficiency
attenuates the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME). Does
TMEM175 directly modulate TAM polarisation? What are the underlying
molecular mechanisms? Moreover, the functional contributions of distinct
immune cell populations to the observed anti-tumour effects remain ambiguous.
Depletion of TAMs and T-cells would substantiate these findings.
Response: Thank you for your comment. In order to investigate the mechanisms of
macrophage polarization in Tmem175-/- mice, we applied single-cell sequencing to
analysis the tumor microenvironment in B16-F10 lung metastatic models. Both AMs
and IMs showed up-regulated antigen presentation pathway, which included several
genes coding histocompatibility molecules such as H2-D1, H2-M3, and H2-K1. And
this result was in accordance with our FCM results. In AMs, we found some up-
regulated genes that have been reported to promote M1-like polarization, such as Tlr2,
Irf7, Nlrp3, Malt1, Map3k1, and Nod2. These genes were enriched in pro-inflammatory
pathways such as NOD-like receptor signaling pathway (mmu04621), NF-kappa B
signaling pathway (mmu04064), and MAPK signaling pathway (mmu04010). These
genes were also enriched in GO terms that facilitate immune process and inflammatory
process, such as immune response (GO:0006955), antigen processing and presentation
of peptide antigen via MHC class I (GO:0002474), and inflammatory response
(GO:0006954). In IMs, we also found some up-regulated genes that have been reported
to promote M1-like polarization, such as Gbp2b, Irf7, Irf9, Gbp4, and Tlr9. These genes
were enriched in pro-inflammatory pathways such as NOD-like receptor signaling
pathway (mmu04621), Toll-like receptor signaling pathway (mmu04620), and NF-
kappa B signaling pathway (mmu04064). These genes were also enriched in GO terms
that facilitate immune process and inflammatory process, such as immune system
process (GO:0002376), antigen processing and presentation (GO:0002474), positive
regulation of interleukin-1 beta production (GO:0032731), positive regulation of NF-
kappaB transcription factor activity (GO:0051092). In summary, TMEM175 knockout
promoted the antigen presentation and inflammatory process resulting in the M1-like
polarization of TAMs, which could involve several different pathways including
inflammasome, NF-kappa B, and TLRs.
Additionally, we confirmed that IL-1 modulated the M1-like polarization of
β
macrophages in vitro. Thus the mechanism of inflammasome-mediated M1-like
polarization in Tmem175-/- mice was investigated by single cell transcriptome analysis
and in vitro experiment.
We used clodronate liposomes to delete macrophages and anti-CD8 antibody to delete
CD8+ T cells to substantiate their roles in the anti-tumor immunity in Tmem175-/- mice.
Clodronate liposomes and anti-CD8 antibody abrogated the differences of tumor
weights between WT and Tmem175-/- mice. Furthermore, clodronate liposomes
inhibited the T cell immunity in Tmem175-/- mice. Thus macrophage deletion smoothed
the differences of immune microenvironment between WT and Tmem175-/- mice.

3. An enigmatic observation lies in the insensitivity of B16-F10 tumours to
inflammasome inhibition (via VX-765) juxtaposed with their heightened
sensitivity to inflammasome stimulation (through chitosan), as illustrated in
Figure 4.
Response: Thank you for your comment. We speculate that inflammasome signal was
seldom activated in B16-F10 tumors from WT mice. It is reasonable that the untreated
state with little inflammasome signal showed insensitivity to inflammasome inhibition
and sensitivity to inflammasome stimulation. To confirm our hypothesis, we used IHC
to investigate the markers of inflammasome signal in B16-F10 tumors from WT and
Tmem175-/- mice. We found that WT B16-F10 tumors showed significantly lower
caspase-1 p10 and IL-1 expression level. Thus it could explain why WT B16-F10
β
tumors were not sensitive to VX-765, because the signal was too low at untreated state.

4. The antigen cross-presentation data presented in Figure 5 are perplexing.
Tmem175-/- bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) markedly induce
proliferation of OVA-specific CD8+ T cells, even in the absence of B16-F10 OVA
cell debris. The addition of B16-F10 OVA debris results in only a minimal further
increase in T cell proliferation. This suggests that the observed T cell proliferation
and activation may occur via mechanisms beyond antigen cross-presentation.
Response: Thank you for your comment. We used RNA-seq to investigate the
underlying mechanisms. We found that in the absence of B16-F10-OVA cell debris,
Tmem175-/- group up-regulated molecules (such as Tlr13, Tlr8, Malt1, Irf4, Irf5, Trim29,
Pcbp2, Cd9, Sema4a) that have been reported to promote T cell proliferation and
activation. And these genes were enriched in innate immune response (GO:0045087),
immune response (GO:0006955 adaptive immune response (GO:0002250) , and
inflammatory response (GO:0006954). Besides antigen specific T cell proliferation and
activation, the non-specific T cell proliferation and activation through theses
inflammation signal might exist in Tmem175-/- group. We speculate that Tmem175-/-
BMDMs demonstrated pro-inflammatory phenotypes thus promoting non-specific T
cell proliferation and activation. In fact, the inflammatory signals have been reported
to promote T cell proliferation (PMID: 31405895, PMID: 35309296, and PMID:
34772757). In B16-F10-OVA debris treated Tmem175-/- group, cell cycle
(GO:0007049), cell division (GO:0051301), and mitotic spindle organization
(GO:0007052) were up-regulated, which might be attributed to the more robust antigen
specific T cell proliferation induced by Tmem175-/- BMDMs.

2. The authors raise three hypotheses about how TMEM175 deficiency leads to
increased inflammasome activation: increased cathepsin B leakage, higher ROS
levels, and elevated cytosolic calcium. Although all three mechanisms may result
from TMEM175-induced lysosomal dysfunction, the effects of inhibitors (CA-074,
BAPTA-AM, etc) for these pathways on blocking inflammasome activation should
be evaluated to identify whether there’s a dominant pathway responsible for the
pro-inflammatory phenotype in TMEM175 KO macrophages. Moreover, the
dominant inhibitor should be tested in vivo for the effect of pathways on anti-
tumor immunity and tumor growth. VX-765 is only a general inhibitor of
caspase-1. For the precise machinery of anti-tumor immunity, siRNA-mediated
gene silencing in macrophages should be conducted to verify the pharmacological
inhibition data, and the anti-tumor effect of macrophage conditional depletion of
the predominant pathway should be evaluated in vivo. In this way, the manuscript
becomes more focused on a predominant pathways as the key mechanism
underlying their phenotype. By evaluating all types of pathways in superficial
ways, it leaves more to be desired and confuses the reader.
Response: Thank you for your comment. Intratumoral injection of CA-074 and
BAPTA-AM inhibited the anti-tumor immunity in Tmem175-/- mice. Both CA-074 and
BAPTA-AM significantly inhibited the anti-tumor immunity. However, the inhibitory
effects were more obvious in BAPTA-AM group than that in CA-074 group. Thus the
elevated cytosolic calcium seemed to be the dominant pathway responsible for the pro-
inflammatory phenotype in Tmem175-/- macrophages.
